Optimality theory in evolution evaluates traits based on cost-benefit trade-offs relative to alternatives, not simply whether benefits exceed costs or whether traits are always beneficial regardless of cost.  
- (A) is incomplete because it ignores comparison with alternative traits.  
- (C) is incorrect because beneficial traits are not always worth the cost if alternatives yield higher net benefit.  
- (D) is too narrow; traits can persist if they are neutral or if constraints prevent better alternatives, not only if they improve fitness.  
- (B) correctly captures the idea that the trait with the best benefit-to-cost ratio compared to alternatives will be favored.  

Final answer: (B)
